key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search found 58 stable CuI-based ternary compounds that could act as p-type transparent conductors, revealing that tetrahedral coordination and halide chemistry can still support transparent hole transport.
engineering_relevance: These candidates expand the materials palette for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by offering potentially conductive, optically transparent p-type layers.
method: Minima hopping structure search over X–Cu–I ternary compounds
Density functional theory screening for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and low hole effective mass
Revisit of chemical modulation of the valence band design rules using the computed dataset
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, including 49 new compounds and 20 degenerate semiconductors, with Cu2FI2 highlighted as having a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: Predictions are computational and require experimental synthesis and measurements to confirm stability, transparency, and p-type conductivity under real processing conditions.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
